name: Classic
description: The native platform look, with MM-Companion's own semantic tints. Follows the operating system's light/dark setting.
_colors: Values reading 'palette(role)' are Qt stylesheet expressions resolved at paint time from the OS palette — that is how this preset stays light/dark aware without naming a single surface colour. A wash cannot be derived from one (see theme.wash), so any token a translucent fill is taken from must be a literal #rrggbb.

colors._scene.enemy: Who a creature on the Scene is to the table, as the colour of its card's edge. Four because a GM's answer is four: something to fight, something on your side, something that has not decided, and one of the players. They are the board's only colour and they carry a fact nothing else on the card does, so they want to be four colours a glance can tell apart in this preset - not four shades of one.
colors._tint.warning: Was #d1a01e, which only ever existed as a literal in two widget files and so never went through the contrast pass the other tints did: it read at 2.10:1 on a light window, well under the 3.0 floor. Retuned to clear 3.48:1 on both, in the same band as its neighbours, and kept amber rather than orange so the PL-breach marker stays distinct from the red flaw tint beside it.

_metrics: Pixels unless noted. A four-number value is a (left, top, right, bottom) box, read via theme.box().

metrics._space.xxs: Tighter than the smallest ordinary gap: the spacing inside a stacked readout whose rows are one quantity read down a column (the System block's speed lines, movement modes and Power Level limits), where an ordinary gap reads as three separate facts instead of one list.
metrics._space.indent: How far a group card insets the members drawn inside it, so the nesting is legible without a second frame.
metrics._die.padding: The flat button's chrome around the drawing, so the button is die.size + this on each axis. It is what keeps the die from sitting flush against the readout under it.
metrics._compact.width: The size the window opens at in compact mode, before the user resizes it. The minimums are deliberately far below the roller's own content: past them the die and the history simply scroll, which is what lets the mini window be shoved into a corner of a shared screen.
metrics._compact.button: The diameter of the round button that floats over the roller's bottom-right corner and is the only way in and out of compact mode. Big enough to be found without hunting, small enough that the slice of roll history it covers is one card's corner.
metrics._column.mode-toggle: The height of one segment of a card's segmented switch (Independent / Array / Dynamic array / Linked). Set rather than left to the label, so lighting a segment bold never re-heights the strip.
metrics._gm.damage-button: The diameter of one round degree-of-failure button on a GM card's damage row. Small: four of them plus a caption share the width of a 210px card, and the row repeats on every creature on the board.
metrics._gm.card.min: The narrowest a GM card's own column may get. A floor, not the width: a card measures what its damage ladder, its condition button and (expanded) its 96px portrait actually need, the window takes the widest of those across the block, and every card in the block wears it - so the cards still line up in columns of the wrapping flow while the block is only as wide as its fattest card needs.
metrics._gm.pin-strip.min: The pinned strip's floor and ceiling, in pixels. The strip used to be a flat 150 whatever was on it, which is most of a card's width spent on 'Dodge 12'. It measures its widest chip now and clamps between these: the floor keeps the strip's header and its '+' reachable on an empty strip, and the cap is the old fixed width, so nothing is ever wider than it used to be.
metrics._gm.thumb: The portrait on a collapsed GM card. Big enough to tell two goons apart at a glance and to be an easy click target, since it is still the only thing that opens the sheet.
metrics._float.min-width: How small a block popped out into its own window may be dragged. The same bargain the mini roller strikes above: the block lives in a scroll area, so past this it scrolls both ways rather than being clipped, and a popped-out block can be shrunk to a tile beside somebody else's application.
metrics._block.min-extent: How small a docked block may be dragged before it stops shrinking. Small on purpose: the grid is the user's, and a block dragged to a sliver reflows as far as it can and then scrolls inside its own frame rather than refusing. This is the floor of the frame itself, so it wants to be about the height of a title bar — enough that a block squashed to nothing can still be found and dragged back open.
metrics._grid.handle: The thickness of a divider between two blocks, in pixels. It is the grab target for every resize on the page, so it has to be wide enough to hit without being a visible gutter.
metrics._grid.detent: How much resistance a divider meets at a block's recommended size, in pixels. The handle sticks there and needs a deliberate extra pull to go past, so nobody crosses it by accident and everybody can find their way back to it. Zero turns the detent off.

_typography: Point sizes, applied with QFont.setPointSizeF — never as a stylesheet font-size, which would outrank the widget font and break the power card's switched-off transition. A null family keeps the platform default.
_blocks: Per-block size overrides layered over ui/block_sizes.json. Empty here: Classic keeps the shipped sizes.
_assets: Which bundled drawing the die and the hero-point pips are taken from. These are variant ids owned by ui/svg_assets.py, not file paths — a preset picks a look, it cannot point the renderer at an arbitrary file. Classic keeps the plain outlined artwork the app shipped with; the designed presets take the shaded medallion set. Already-built icons are not re-drawn by a stylesheet, so a switch shows up after the relaunch the Settings window offers.
